title: Delegated Claude children inherit every user/project MCP server (no --strict-mcp-config)
outcome: Observed live 2026-09-02: each delegated Claude child is spawned with --setting-sources user,project,local (claude_args.rs push_claude_cli_common_args) and a private --mcp-config for termal-delegation, without --strict-mcp-config. Result: every reviewer child also starts the operator's user-level MCP servers — on this machine two chrome-devtools trees per child (~124+63+86 MB each) started at 01:39:09/:25/:26 — although the injected delegation prompt tells the child not to use browser/Chrome DevTools/external MCP tools. This is a per-child memory multiplier (~270 MB per reviewer), slows child startup, and widens the tool surface of read-only reviewers beyond what TermAl authorizes. Expected: delegation children run with a TermAl-owned strict MCP set (termal-delegation plus explicitly allowed servers such as Engram when the delegation opts in), e.g. --strict-mcp-config with the private --mcp-config, while root interactive sessions keep inheriting user settings. Verify against the current Claude CLI contract for --strict-mcp-config semantics before changing; keep the Codex delegation MCP baseline aligned. No Beads IDs in code comments.
